title: The Second Ray of Fading Light
next_chapter_hook: The fragmented soul of the ruins' guardian whispered like a serpent drilling into his ear: 'The power of choice never rests in a chess piece's hands—what you believe to be choices are merely movements upon my board.'

text.content: Chen Ji's footsteps came to an abrupt halt, as if nailed to the ground by that aged voice. The surrounding air suddenly solidified, an indescribable pressure sweeping from the depths of the ruins, carrying the vicissitudes and weight of eons past. His pupils contracted slightly—this voice was identical to the first generation Chess Player recorded in the Tianji Record Fragment. That forbidden existence that had perished in ancient times—was it actually speaking to him now?

dialogue.content: 'You have finally arrived... I have been waiting, for a very long time.' The voice sounded again, no longer a distant ethereal whisper, but an intimate murmur at his side, as if invisible hands were gently stroking the back of his neck. 'My inheritor, the next Chess Player of the Tianji Record—you arrived faster than I anticipated.'

text.content: Chen Ji did not move. His breathing was eerily steady, yet his heart hammered like drums within his chest. Inheritor? He sneered inwardly. He had witnessed too many flowery packages concealing thorns—behind every so-called 'inheritance' lay bloody costs. Yet curiosity compelled him to slowly turn, his gaze falling upon the source of the voice—where a ruin vastly different from the previous one was gradually manifesting from the void.

If what he had witnessed moments ago was a palace of light, then what now emerged was an abyss of darkness. Black jade formed towers, each block emanating a cold, eerie glow. Countless runes densely carved upon the tower's surface were twisted and sinister, remarkably similar yet fundamentally opposed to the patterns of the Tianji Record. Chen Ji felt the fragment in his mind suddenly jolt, as if responding to some kind of summoning.

dialogue.content: 'Do you see?' The voice carried a near-pitying smile. 'The first path leads to the Eye of Heavenly Dao, becoming its chess piece, battling on its board until the last drop of your value is wrung dry. And this second path—' the voice paused, 'is to take its place.'

text.content: To take its place. Chen Ji's pupils sharply contracted. The word sliced through to his deepest desires like a keen blade. To become the Chess Player, gazing down upon all beings, using heaven and earth as a chessboard, all living creatures as chess pieces—wasn't this the very power he had always dreamed of? Yet a mocking curve crept onto his lips. There is never a free lunch in this world, and the more tempting the fruit, often the more potent the poison.

The black tower's doors silently opened, an air of decay and majesty rushing to meet him. Chen Ji stepped inside, and the scene before him stole his breath—murals. A massive mural covering an entire wall, depicting the Chess Player's supreme dominion. Mountains and rivers spanning countless miles beneath his fingertips, all living beings prostrating like ants, countless immortals and deities submitting meekly, not daring to meet his gaze even for a moment.

Yet at the mural's end was an entirely different scene. The same Chess Player, imprisoned by chains in the endless void, eyes hollow, flesh long rotted to bones, only a wisp of obsession still struggling defiantly. Around him were countless similarly imprisoned souls, each once as spirited and ambitious as he, each meeting the same fate.

'Eternal power, eternal solitude.' The voice followed like a shadow. 'Become the Chess Player, and you shall possess the power to rewrite heaven and earth, but the price is—you can never leave this board. You will watch those you love depart one by one, while you remain trapped here until eternity.' Chen Ji felt a bone-deep chill. He thought of Chen Nian, of Su Qingyao, of all those he had yet to protect.

text.content: Chen Ji did not avoid those hollow sockets in the mural; instead, he stepped forward, a playful smile curling his lips. 'Imprisonment? Interesting. Pray tell, Elder, were these chains imposed by the Eye of Heavenly Dao, or... did the Chess Player forge them himself?' The words fell, and the surrounding atmosphere shifted dramatically. The aged laughter rang out again, but now carried a note of approval.

text.content: Chen Ji stepped back, his gaze cold and sharp as a blade. 'Elder's kindness, Chen acknowledges. But there is never a free meal in this world—what you call 'taking its place' is merely another cage.' His voice was cold yet resolute. 'Chen would rather be a chess piece for a lifetime than a prisoner for eternity.'

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly let out a light laugh, the smile carrying a hint of world-weary cunning: 'Senior, the two paths you mentioned—one is being a dog, the other is being a caged king. Chen ventures to ask—is there a third path? One where one is neither a dog nor locked away?' The air seemed to freeze for a moment, then that ancient voice let out a meaningful chuckle.

'Clever.' The voice finally showed a hint of genuine appreciation. 'No wonder you are the one the Tianji Record chose. Unlike other candidates who were drunk on power, you didn't flee like a coward either.' The skeletal remains on the mural seemed to tremble slightly, and a ghostly green light shot from those hollow eye sockets, shining directly on Chen Ji. 'But have you considered—that these two paths might be different stages of the same road?'

Chen Ji frowned, alarm bells ringing in his heart. The same road? What did that mean? Could becoming a chess piece of the Eye of Heavenly Dao ultimately lead to a prisoner's cage? Or... he abruptly looked up, his gaze sharp as lightning: 'Senior, are you saying the Eye of Heavenly Dao is itself a prisoner?' The surroundings fell into deathly silence. That ghostly green light trembled violently, as if stabbed in a sore spot.

The earlier world-weary attitude vanished, replaced by a suffocating sharpness: 'Since we've come this far, senior, might as well speak plainly—who is the Eye of Heavenly Dao? How many pieces truly move on its chessboard?' The ghostly green light abruptly stalled, then transformed into a long, drawn-out sigh.

But this matter carries great weight—may I ask the senior to explain what the chess player's inheritance actually entails?' The voice fell silent for a moment, seemingly examining his sincerity, before slowly speaking: 'You are indeed far more cautious than those fools.'

text.content: Chen Ji said nothing, standing with hands clasped behind his back, his gaze calm as an abyss. The guardian seemed to be waiting precisely for this composure, its laughter growing increasingly eerie: "Good, very good. The more composed you are, the more I believe you are that person. Since you asked, I'll tell you—the Heavenly Eye, it is both the oldest chess player and the one who has been imprisoned the longest."

The Heavenly Eye, it is both the oldest chess player and the one who has been imprisoned the longest. These words exploded in Chen Ji's mind like thunder. He suddenly understood—perhaps the so-called Heavenly Eye was never some transcendent will at all, but an existence that longed to break free more than anyone else. It needed pieces, needed fresh blood, needed someone to walk upon the chessboard on its behalf...

"So that's why it set these two paths." Chen Ji murmured to himself, his eyes flickering with sharp light, "One path makes people willingly become pieces, the other makes people think they can take the opponent's place—but no matter which path, in the end, it will get fresh nourishment. It doesn't care who becomes the chess player; it only cares... that this game cannot stop." The枯骨 on the mural suddenly burst forth with blinding light, and that ancient voice turned sharp and凌厉: "You are very clever, clever enough to make me feel afraid."

The Heavenly Eye needs you to maintain the chessboard's operation, so it will never let you leave. But if someone could break this cycle... you would finally achieve true liberation, would you not?" The枯骨 on the mural trembled slightly, that eerie green light showing hints of urgency.

text.content: Chen Ji performed a proper bow, his posture composed and appropriate: "Many thanks for Senior's guidance; Chen has greatly benefited. However, Chen still has some minor matters to attend to, so I won't trouble you further." He turned to leave, but his feet seemed nailed to the ground—that was the guardian's pressure, cold and heavy. "Do you think knowing these things allows you to walk away unscathed?" That voice finally shed all pretense.

Chen Ji's footsteps halted, but he didn't look back. His voice was calm to the point of indifference: "What does Senior mean by this? Chen merely listened to a story—could even walking away be forbidden?" That ancient laughter rang out again, but now with a chilling edge: "Do you think this is a business transaction? Listen to the story and then leave without a care?" The runes within the black tower suddenly lit up, and dense chains emerged from the void, slowly approaching Chen Ji.

Chen Ji finally turned around. There was not a trace of fear on his face; instead, he wore a meaningful smile: "Senior, you're impatient." The approaching chains hesitated momentarily. "You've been trapped here too long, too long, to the point of losing even basic patience. You need Chen, need someone who can break the chessboard—but the more anxious you become, the more it shows that this chessboard... is already collapsing." The枯骨 on the mural suddenly erupted with blinding green light, the voice becoming savage and distorted: "Clever! Too clever! Clever enough that I must kill you now!"

At this critical moment, the Tianji Record Fragment in Chen Ji's mind violently trembled. An unprecedented surge of information flooded his consciousness—so that's it! The so-called chess player inheritance was never some gift of power, but a... sacrifice! Every generation of chess players' fall would transform their Heavenly Fate and obsession into nourishment, feeding that which existed in the darkness. And the Heavenly Eye was merely the... watchdog of this sacrifice! Chen Ji felt a chill crawl from his tailbone to the top of his head.

"So this is your true purpose." Chen Ji's voice echoed through the Black Tower, clear and resolute. "You don't want to help Chen become a Chess Player at all. You want to make Chen... the next sacrifice. You told Chen the truth not out of kindness, but because only by knowing these things will Chen do one of two things—and whichever path Chen chooses, it's a dead end. And your fragmented soul can take this chance to escape this prison!" The skeletal remains on the mural froze completely, and the countless chains hung suspended in mid-air, as if immobilized by some unseen force.

A deathly silence descended within the Black Tower. The guardian's voice rang out once more, no longer the cold, menacing tone from before, but carrying an inexplicable complexity: "So you are indeed the one it chose... No, to be precise, you are someone even it couldn't fully comprehend." The skeletal remains on the mural slowly closed their hollow eye sockets, and the eerie green glow gradually faded away. "Since you know everything now, then as you wish—go. But remember, the right of choice has never been in a chess piece's hands. You think you're making a choice, but you're merely moving on my chessboard."
